question: What will be the SPIMEX exchange settlement price of AI-95 gasoline on October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class is the daily SPIMEX AI-95 index 13 days ahead in the 2026 strike-disrupted regime; a random walk off the current level is the anchor (~71.8k as of Sep 18). The Aug 20 record of 82,253 has retraced ~13%, but the decline flattened over Sep 8-18 (-2% then +0.2% w/w), so the status-quo outcome is a plateau near 71-72k on Oct 1. Downward: refiners resuming, crude -9.5% in four sessions, post-summer demand, shrinking exchange volumes and buyers deterred by months-long delivery delays. Upward: Yaroslavl halted Sep 17 with its isomerization (high-octane) unit hit, Saratov and Syzran struck, regional rationing - AI-95-specific scarcity supports a spike tail, and 2025 saw a late-Sept/early-Oct record after a similar lull. Slight right skew accordingly. Extra variance from index ambiguity: sources give 71.4k (national) vs 72.2k (European territorial) vs 68.8k (volume-weighted European) for the same session, and TASS's headlined figure is only loosely identified. No prediction market prices this, so the number is unblended.

Earlier 2026 reference points: 63,370 on Feb 13 (Kommersant); 65,049 in March (TASS); 75,576 on Jun 19 after a -7.42% week (finance.mail.ru); AI-95 +~4% in the week to Jul 18 (brief24).

BASE RATES / DISPERSION, with the class each is computed over: (a) over ALL 13-14 day windows in the Jun-Sep 2026 series that I could price: Aug 20->Sep 1 -7.7%, Aug 28->Sep 11 -5.7%, Sep 4->Sep 18 -2.4% - i.e. every measurable two-week window since the August peak was negative, magnitudes shrinking monotonically. (b) over weekly windows in 2026: range roughly -7.4% (week to Jun 19) to +4% (week to Jul 18). (c) CONDITIONAL on the most recent two weeks only (the post-plateau regime): -2.0% then +0.2%, i.e. near-zero drift with ~1-2% weekly noise. (d) Seasonal analogue, over the single comparable prior year: in 2025 AI-95 first passed 80,000 on Aug 8, dipped to 78,700 on Sep 15, then returned to 80,000 on Oct 2 - a mid-September lull followed by an early-October rise (Kommersant, Oct 2, 2025).

SUPPLY / POLICY EVIDENCE BOTH DIRECTIONS: gasoline export ban runs to Jan 31, 2027 (announced Jul 30, 2026), keeping volumes domestic. Mandatory exchange-sale norm was cut from 15% to 10% of output, shrinking the buyer pool from hundreds to dozens and cutting session volumes (Moscow Times, Sep 8). Refiners have failed to complete shipment on nearly 60% of May-Sep exchange contracts, with delivery postponements of several months; buyers are stepping back from contracts with uncertain delivery, which decouples exchange quotes from physical scarcity (Moscow Times, Sep 8). Sep 14-18 AI-95 session volume averaged 4,032 t, -10.4% w/w and -25% vs August; AI-92 7,320 t, +1.3% w/w, -13% vs August (Moscow Times, Sep 18). Against that: Ukrainian strikes in the week of Sep 14-18 hit Saratov, Syzran and Yaroslavl; Yaroslavl halted around Sep 17, having lost a further ~40% of capacity on top of ~33% still under repair from an Aug 28 strike, with a distillation tower, storage tanks and an isomerization unit (high-octane blendstock) damaged (bne IntelliNews / Sep 21 open-source summaries); estimates of 30-40% of Russian refining capacity offline circulate, with regional shortages and coupon rationing reported in some areas. Regional workarounds are being set up that bypass the exchange: Stavropol Krai announced on Sep 21 an agreement letting filling-station networks buy directly from refiners, explicitly to 'reduce the influence of exchange purchases on final fuel cost', plus a 6% markup cap, with extra AI-92/AI-95 volumes being delivered and stabilisation expected by early October. Mishustin authorised refineries to drop from Euro-5 to Euro-3 gasoline spec through year-end (Jul 2, 2026), expanding sellable volume. Crude backdrop: front-month Nymex WTI settled $95.78 on Sep 21, -4.51% on the day and -9.5% over four sessions, though still +67% YTD; Russian domestic wholesale is only loosely coupled to it via the damper mechanism. Retail: Russian pump prices eased from ~$0.93/l in July to ~$0.87-0.88/l in mid-September (GlobalPetrolPrices/dailyfuels); B1 analysts see retail +1-2% per month to year-end (Vedomosti, Aug 26).

MARKETS: searched Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi and bookmakers for any contract on SPIMEX or Russian wholesale gasoline prices - none found; the harness title search also returned no candidate. No crowd anchor exists for this quantity.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: any AI-95 exchange print for Sep 19-21, 2026 (the latest confirmed session figure is Sep 18); SPIMEX's own index page or a machine-readable daily history (spimex.com/spimex.global not retrievable in this run); an explicit statement of which named SPIMEX index TASS uses in its daily English report; any published SPIMEX trading calendar confirming or denying an Oct 1 session beyond the question's own assertion that it is a scheduled trading day; any analyst forecast specifically for the wholesale AI-95 exchange price at end-September/early-October 2026.

calls.reconciliation: Three disputes were factual. (a) Run 1's claim that 71,417 and 72,167 are two same-day indices is wrong: Runs 2 and 3 both date 72,167 to Sep 11 and 71,417 to Sep 18, so that is a time series, not a basis split - index ambiguity is narrower than Run 1 priced, leaving only the lone gknefteprodukt 68,823 aggregator variant. (b) The Aug 31 80,167 vs Sep 1 74,121/75,926 conflict could not be settled without web access; I treat it as likely a national-vs-territorial basis difference and carry it as ~2% of dispersion rather than resolving it by fiat. (c) Sessions remaining is 8 (Sep 22-Oct 1 inclusive), not 7; immaterial. On judgment: I took Run 2's octane-spread-compression argument as the strongest unpriced asymmetry but drew the opposite conclusion from it than Run 2 did, landing the median just above all three runs at 71,900 rather than below; and I set p_below_lower at 0.05, rejecting Run 3's 0.12 because the only in-sample precedent for a -9% two-week move is the spent post-record mean-reversion phase. I adopt the runs' shared reference class (last print as random-walk anchor) and a dispersion between Run 2's and Run 3's.
